Positive Points

Sensient Technologies Corp (NYSE:SXT) reported a strong start to 2026 with 7% local currency revenue growth, 10% local currency adjusted EBITDA growth, and 14% local currency adjusted EPS growth. The Color Group delivered impressive results with 12.3% local currency revenue growth and 13.2% local currency operating profit growth. The Asia Pacific Group showed a strong rebound with 4.7% local currency revenue growth and 14.5% local currency operating profit growth. Q: Paul, the first quarter results exceeded expectations. Can you provide more details on what drove this performance? Was it faster customer conversions or inventory build-up? A: Paul Manning, CEO: The primary driver was more wins than anticipated, particularly in natural color conversions and general business. Q: Regarding the growth cadence for the Color Group, how should we expect it to unfold throughout the year? A: Paul Manning, CEO: Q2 should look similar to Q1 across all groups. The process involves significant reformulation and production adjustments.

Q: On margins for the Color Group, are you expecting them to be flat or improve throughout the year? A: Paul Manning, CEO: We expect EBITDA margins to be flat for the year. Investments in capital and personnel are ongoing, but revenue inflow timing will impact margins. We aim to be early on capital implementation to support future growth.

title: Why Sensient Technologies Stock Soared on Friday
content:
Key Points

The company is benefiting from a trend towards the use of natural flavors. Its valuations don't look all that compelling, however.10 stocks we like better than Sensient Technologies ›

An estimates-crushing quarter was the spark that lit a fire under Sensient Technologies(NYSE: SXT) as the stock trading week came to a close. The rather under-the-radar company, which specializes in flavors, colors, and extracts used across industries such as food and pharmaceuticals, saw its shares rise by a meaty 24% on Friday.

One tasty quarter

Sensient booked revenue of just under $436 million in its first quarter, for a year-over-year improvement of more than 11%. Better, the company's net income under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) rocketed 28% higher to almost $44.2 million, or $1.04 per share.

Both headline numbers were more than high enough to trounce the consensus analyst estimates. Professional Sensient trackers were modeling just over $411 million for the quarter's revenue, and a mere $0.83 for per-share, GAAP net income.

Sensient breaks its business down into two product categories. Of the two, color saw the more robust revenue growth -- its take grew by 18% compared to the 4% of flavors and extracts.

That outperformance might become a habit. In its earnings release, the company said that strong demand for natural flavor products was a particular driver of growth during the period.

Enhanced guidance

It was a beat-and-raise quarter for Sensient, as it adjusted several of its full-year 2026 projections. Management now expects non-GAAP (adjusted) revenue to grow at a high single-digit to double-digit percentage rate compared to 2025; previously, it forecast mid-single-digit to double-digit growth.

As for GAAP profitability, its new guidance is for $3.70 to $3.90 per share for the year. This betters the previous estimate of $3.60 to $3.80.

While every investor dreams of discovering and snapping up a "sleeper stock," Sensient's valuations look a little rich to me just now (its price/sales is 2.6, while forward P/E is almost 23). I don't feel it's a serious bargain, especially after Friday's pop, so I'd probably leave the stock alone for now.

title: Sensient Technologies Corporation Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Sensient Technologies Corporation Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers

Performance exceeded early expectations driven by high win rates in natural colors and technically differentiated products in the Color Group. Management identifies the U.S. wholesale conversion from synthetic to natural colors as the single largest opportunity in the company's history. The Color Group's 12.3% local currency growth was split roughly equally between base business strength and incremental natural color conversion revenue. Customer service levels remain exceptionally high despite a sluggish global food market, positioning the firm to capture market share through innovation. Natural color conversions are viewed as manageable for customers because color remains a relatively small portion of total ingredient costs in most categories. The Asia Pacific Group saw a substantial rebound as regional demand constraints improved and new sales wins accelerated faster than anticipated. Operational focus remains on building a resilient botanical supply chain to support customer launch dates and the $1 billion natural color sales goal.

Outlook and Strategic Assumptions

Guidance was raised to reflect high single to double-digit local currency revenue and EBITDA growth, assuming continued momentum in the back half of 2026. Management expects a decided inflection point for natural color conversions in Q4 2026 as customers finalize reformulation and move toward 2027 deadlines. Consolidated capital expenditures are projected at $150 million to $170 million for 2026, while the company expects to spend $225 million to $250 million specifically on natural color capital over the next couple of years. The company anticipates taking modest price increases in the low single digits to mitigate inflationary pressures from fuel, logistics, and petroleum-based inputs. Leverage is expected to increase toward the upper 2s later in the year as the company builds inventory to support anticipated conversion volume.

Risk Factors and Market Dynamics

Geopolitical conflict in Iran is being monitored for supply chain risks; management expects to mitigate fuel and commodity price increases through pricing actions. The phase-out of titanium dioxide (TiO2) represents a significant technical challenge and a growing global market opportunity not yet factored into the $1 billion goal. Regulatory pressures and retailer-driven deadlines, such as Walmart's January 2027 target, are serving as primary catalysts for the industry's conversion timeline. Interest expense is expected to rise by approximately $6 million for the full year due to increased debt levels associated with capital investments.

Q&A Highlights

Drivers of first quarter outperformance and win rates

The beat was primarily driven by higher-than-anticipated wins in both the base business and natural color conversions. Management noted that tariff distortions feared in previous quarters moderated, contributing to the stronger results.

Customer commitment and potential for conversion delays

Management expressed extreme confidence in the timeline, stating they have seen no slowdown or deviation in customer commitment over the last six months. Large CPG companies are currently in the complex phase of aligning production plans, consumer testing, and regulatory reviews for dozens of product lines.

Quantifying the natural color conversion progress

Approximately $20 million has been invoiced toward the $1 billion natural color conversion goal over the last nine months. Management expects the conversion pace to accelerate as the industry nears a 'tipping point' where competitive pressure forces rapid adoption.

Impact of FDA regulatory activity on the color toolbox

approximately half this growth was due to natural color conversions.Color Group adjusted EBITDA margin -- 24.4%, flat to prior year, reflecting ongoing investment for natural color conversion activity.Color Group outlook -- Management now expects double-digit local currency revenue growth for 2026, a step up from previous high single-digit to double-digit guidance.Flavors & Extracts Group revenue -- Gained 1.7% in local currency, while operating profit grew 5.1%; adjusted EBITDA margin improved 30 basis points to 17.2%.Asia Pacific Group revenue -- Achieved 4.7% local currency growth and 14.5% local currency operating profit growth; adjusted EBITDA margin rose 220 basis points to 26.1%.Natural color invoicing -- $20 million invoiced over the past nine months toward the $1 billion U.S. natural color conversion goal.Updated guidance -- Local currency revenue now expected to rise high single-digit to double-digit; adjusted EBITDA and EPS both guided to high single-digit to double-digit local currency growth.Capital expenditures -- On track for $150 million to $170 million in 2026, including $225 million to $250 million targeted for natural color investments over the next two years.Net debt to credit adjusted EBITDA -- 2.4 times as of Mar. 31, 2026, with expectations for leverage to increase into the upper two times range through year-end due to higher inventories for natural color production.Interest expense -- $7.9 million in the first quarter, up from $7.3 million the prior year, with second quarter guidance of $9 million.Adjusted effective tax rate -- 24.9% for the quarter, with guidance for 25% in the second quarter and for the full year.Foreign currency EPS benefit -- Aided adjusted EPS by $0.06 in the first quarter; overall currency expected to be immaterial for full-year results.Cash flow from operations -- $(14) million used in the quarter, reflecting planned inventory investments ahead of increased natural color demand.Major strategic priority -- Management reaffirmed the wholesale conversion of synthetic colors to natural colors in the U.S. as the company’s "single largest opportunity."Competitive landscape -- Management noted, "there is no slowdown at any of these customers," and "there is no deviation from...they will do this," regarding synthetic to natural color conversion commitments.Cost pass-through and input inflation -- Price increases in the low single-digit range are anticipated to offset expected raw material and logistics inflation, especially in synthetics.Share buybacks -- Not anticipated at this time; ongoing evaluation of "sensible acquisition opportunities" continues.Regulatory milestones -- The U.S. Walmart deadline of Jan. 1, 2027, and a broader industry target of Jan. 1, 2028, are cited as timeline anchors for customer conversions.

Risks

Management highlighted inflationary pressures, citing, "there is a sufficient amount of inflationary inputs that we're going to need to take pricing to address that," especially in synthetics and logistics.Interest expense is expected to rise by approximately $6 million for the full year, with leverage ratio guidance indicating higher debt usage as natural color investments ramp.Management stated, "Our leverage ratio right now is about 2.4. In our comments, I mentioned, we expect that to climb as our debt increases throughout the year. So we'll be in the higher two times from that point."Geopolitical and input cost risks remain under review; management is monitoring the Iran conflict, warning, "we are working to mitigate any potential supply chain risks that may result from the overall increase in fuel and certain commodity prices."

Summary

Sensient Technologies(NYSE:SXT) reported 7% local currency revenue growth, 10% local currency adjusted EBITDA growth, and 14% local currency adjusted EPS growth, driven by both core business strengths and accelerating U.S. natural color conversions. Management increased full-year revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS guidance to high single-digit to double-digit local currency growth, citing "exceptionally high" customer commitment and new sales pipeline momentum. Interest expense and capital spending are projected to climb, raising leverage as the company invests heavily in production capacity and inventory to capture forecasted natural color demand. Supply chain resilience, regulatory deadlines, and proactive pricing measures were explicitly framed as strategic levers to counter industry inflation and potential disruptions, particularly related to geopolitical events and cost escalation in both synthetic and natural color inputs.

Management said, "we have about $100 million of synthetic colors, and we think that will convert at about ten to one," confirming a substantial addressable market for the natural color transition.Large retailers' deadlines and competitive dynamics are driving the timing of customer conversions, with management noting an industry "tipping point" may accelerate transitions beyond current expectations.The Color Group's pipeline for natural color conversions "continues to look very promising," with approximately half of segment growth directly attributed to these conversions in the recent quarter.Ongoing investments in the Avalanche platform and extrusion-stable natural colors address customer demand for titanium dioxide (TiO2) alternatives and compliance with evolving regulations.Capital allocation prioritizes natural color production capacity, with no share repurchases planned, and continued discipline toward acquisitions under consideration.

Industry glossary

Natural color conversion: The process of replacing synthetic food and personal care colors with naturally sourced color ingredients, often in response to regulatory, retailer, or consumer demands.Adjusted EBITDA margin: A profitability ratio measuring adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of revenue, used to assess operational efficiency excluding certain one-time or non-cash items.Avalanche platform: Sensient's portfolio of clean label whitening agents designed to replace titanium dioxide (TiO2) in food and personal care applications.TiO2: Titanium dioxide, a whitening additive commonly used in foods, beverages, and cosmetics, increasingly subject to regulatory restrictions and substitution by natural alternatives.

But overall, FX should be about immaterial when you look at it for the year. So -- when you look at it, we did increase our EPS guidance from where we were in Q1. So right now, we're at high single-digit growth and double-digit growth. So that's kind of where we are at this point.

Ming Tang: And then just going back on the previous -- you answered the previous question, I was just reflecting on it. When you said 20 million invoiced -- is that with reference to the EUR 100 million revenue synthetic revenue or the EUR 1 billion overall revenue opportunity?

Tobin Tornehl: The $1 billion. .

Ming Tang: And then the final question would be just around raw materials. You mentioned you don't have significant direct exposure to Middle East, but I think there's a general view that input inflation there may be more input inflation, particularly on the synthetic side. I was wondering what you're expecting in terms of inputs this year? And are we mainly talking about synthetics? Or should we be thinking about certain naturals within your supply chain, which are either sourced I don't know from the Middle East or from Asia or something where there might be a potential disruption either in terms of cost availability?

Paul Manning: So in short, we believe that there is a sufficient amount of inflationary inputs that we're going to need to take pricing to address that. This would be sort of low single-digit magnitude. So not unlike again, where we've done this in other instances of tariffs and wars and pandemics and the like. We would anticipate taking pricing there. The biggest factors here, there's certainly the logistical inflation substantially derived from energy and petroleum more specifically. So we face that. . There's an impact of packaging as many of those raw materials have petroleum-based in inputs.

And then of course, as many in the media are fond of saying, petroleum-based synthetic colors, of course, therefore, you realize that a couple of those synthetic colors are indeed derived. Of course, then again, many things in nature are derived from that as well. But that aside, we would expect to see more on the raw material side of synthetic colors for food and for personal care that we would need to address. For natural colors, it would come sort of fertilizers and other input costs we see rising. So those would have an impact on natural colors. But a lot of these costs for harvest are built into the next year's harvest often time.

You hear me talk about that with our raw materials or with our agricultural business. So in short, there's many of these different factors, but I think we can address this, and we will address this with a modest amount of price increase that we would expect to give principally focused in synthetic colors for food and personal care, but also anything related to logistics, which is effectively all in down and outbound freight. And then, of course, a couple of other -- you'll hear propylene glycol is another one that's been heavily impacted by the war. So that's how we kind of see it playing out right now.

And even if the war were to stop, there's still a sufficient enough backlog in other sources of a nurture here that the inflation is coming if it hasn't already, and so we're going to need to address that.

Operator: The next question is a follow-up from Joshua Spector with UBS.

Joshua Spector: Just a small follow-up and actually related to what you were just talking about, is just as you look at your 2Q guide, are you baking in anything in terms of a negative impact from transport logistics loss, et cetera? Or are you assuming your pricing offsets that more or less in real time?

Paul Manning: I'm not assuming any bad, and I'm not assuming any good. So I didn't assume the inflation because at this point, it's fairly modest and some of it is, quite frankly, deferred. But I'm also not assuming any pricing in Q2. either from a guidance standpoint.

Operator: And that concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mr. Tornehl for any closing remarks. Please go ahead.

Tobin Tornehl: Okay. Thank you for your time today. That concludes our call. If you have any follow-up questions, please feel free to reach out to the company. Have a great weekend.

title: Sensient Technologies (SXT) Q1 Earnings and Revenues Top Estimates
content:
Sensient Technologies (SXT) came out with quarterly earnings of $1.04 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.8 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.86 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +30.00%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this maker of colors, flavors and fragrances would post earnings of $0.78 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.72, delivering a surprise of -7.69%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates just once.

Sensient, which belongs to the Zacks Chemical - Specialty industry, posted revenues of $435.83 million for the quarter ended March 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 7.38%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $392.33 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates just once over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Sensient shares have added about 5.6% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 3.8%.

What's Next for Sensient?

While Sensient has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Sensient was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.94 on $437.8 million in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.70 on $1.73 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Chemical - Specialty is currently in the bottom 38% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Another stock from the same industry, International Flavors (IFF), has yet to report results for the quarter ended March 2026. The results are expected to be released on May 5.

This ingredients producer for food, cosmetics and consumer products industries is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.08 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -10%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 1.5% lower over the last 30 days to the current level.

International Flavors' revenues are expected to be $2.65 billion, down 6.8% from the year-ago quarter.
